findings.claim: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth is raised tenfold from 500 to 5000. This weakens the recursion/depth limit that protects against stack overflow when deserializing untrusted data, and nothing in REQ-2283 (a compile-time generator/analyzer crash) calls for it. Deeply nested payloads could now overflow the stack on threads with small stacks, and the change contradicts the recorded stack depth limit of 500.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a payload nested 600-5000 levels deep (e.g. nested single-element arrays) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). On base this throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; on head it succeeds, or overflows the stack on a small-stack thread. Also assert MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper wraps every reportDiagnostic callback and silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in source or is not in the compilation. A diagnostic with a null or None location, for example one created via Diagnostic.Create with a null Location, is now suppressed instead of surfacing. This could hide analyzer diagnostics that warn about insecure or unsupported configurations, such as MsgPack003/004/005 and others that are Errors. The suppression is broader than the three crash sites.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003-018 verifiers) on head. Add cases where the diagnostic location is Location.None or a different syntax tree (for example a partial type or a type declared in another tree), and check that the expected diagnostics are still reported.
